subject: Updating a ui display from data within the server

messages.author: e8e108c1c1b7357e
messages.subject: Updating a ui display from data within the server
parts: I'm relatively new to R and Shiny, but have already learned a lot and built a fairly large simulation model of a software development process. But, a key element of this simulation is that I need the server code to run in a loop and pass new values to the plots and charts updating them dynamically without user intervention.  Is there a relatively easy way to do this?  (I know I can't update the input$xxx variables via code).

messages.author: 556a11f9dbf4e4a2
messages.subject: Re: Updating a ui display from data within the server
parts:
Hi Michael,

what about running the code in a reactive function that output the results in a dataframe that is subsequently read by the output render function(s)?

something like the following:

dts <- reactive({
  ... simulation model code ...
  broom::tidyr(...) # not essential but can help
})

output$my_plot <- renderPlot({
  ggplot(dts(), ...
})


But without further info about your process, it is very difficult to help. 

And it's not actually true that you can't update input vars: see all the update*Input functions here

Luca

messages.author: e8e108c1c1b7357e
messages.subject: Re: Updating a ui display from data within the server
parts:
Luca,

 

Thanks for the insight, but as I said, I’m very new to all this and creating a reactive function is something I’ll need to research more.  And thanks for pointing me to the update* functions - I didn't know that was possible.

 

Here is a highly minimized concept of what I’m trying to achieve.  A loop, within the server that can update the display in the shiny dashboard:


library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
   
    # Application title
    titlePanel("My Test"),
    
    # Start Sim 
    actionButton(inputId = "start",
                label = "Start"),
    
    # Display status
    mainPanel(
          htmlOutput("f0")
    )
)

# Define server logic 
server <- function(input, output, session) {
   
    observeEvent(input$start, {
        
        for (i in 1:10) {
            
            output$f0 <- renderText({
                paste("Number: ", runif(1,1,10))
            })
            
            invalidateLater(1000, session)
                  
        }
    })
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)




Mikey

messages.subject: Re: Updating a ui display from data within the server
parts:
Hi, 

this should be relatively easy to do, I recently completed a similar project, the difference between what you are doing and what I was doing was user input controlled the way one steppedthrough the simulation. I would write the simulation as a separate function return the needed values and then call this function from within observeEvent this is sort of what you  ar doing in your minimal example anyway.The main difference is that you would need to wrap your loop within a function. Rather than embedding it within observeEvent() directly.

You only really need reactive functions or values if the simulation id dependent on user input.

There is also a question of how you want to display your model on ui, I used tabular output, but have been exploring the possibility of using animation to present graphical output, there appears to be some debate as to whether this is possible or not with Shiny.

R.
